# Disagreement Log — Apocalypse of Peter, Chapter 17
**Agents:** EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Verse-by-Verse Disagreements

### v.1 — "while he was yet speaking" vs. "while he was still speaking"
- **EMET:** "while he was yet speaking"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "while he was still speaking"
- **Note:** "Yet" (EMET) is archaic; "still" (LOGOS) is standard modern English. Minor.

### v.1 — Words on the cloud
- **EMET/LOGOS/PNEUMA:** All agree on the content. PNEUMA adds the words in two sentences; EMET/LOGOS in one. No substantive disagreement.

### v.2 — "weeping and sorrowful" vs. "sorrowful beyond words" (PNEUMA)
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "weeping and sorrowful"
- **PNEUMA:** "weeping. We were sorrowful beyond words"
- **Note:** "Beyond words" is PNEUMA's addition. "Weeping and sorrowful" is sufficient.

### v.3 — "the day of my coming, which is to be completed" vs. "which will be fulfilled"
- **EMET:** "which is to be completed"
- **LOGOS:** "which will be fulfilled"
- **PNEUMA:** "the day that will be fulfilled"
- **Note:** "Fulfilled" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is the better rendering of the eschatological completion.

### v.4 — "draw away from us" vs. "pull away from us"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "draw away from us"
- **PNEUMA:** "pull away from us"
- **Note:** "Draw" is more gentle; "pull" implies force. Minor.

### v.5 — "weeping and lamenting, and they said" vs. "they were weeping... they were lamenting"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** Single clause.
- **PNEUMA:** "They were weeping. They were lamenting." — broken into separate sentences.
- **Note:** PNEUMA's fragmentation for emphasis is a stylistic choice not in source.

### v.7 — "taken from our midst" — all agree.

### v.8 — "proclaimed righteous in his name, sanctified, and their sins were forgiven"
- **EMET:** "were proclaimed righteous in his name and were sanctified and their sins were forgiven them"
- **LOGOS:** "proclaimed righteous in his name, sanctified, and their sins were forgiven them"
- **PNEUMA:** "They were counted righteous in his name. They were made holy."
- **Note:** PNEUMA's "counted righteous" vs. "proclaimed righteous" — minor. "Made holy" vs. "sanctified" — equivalent.

### v.9 — "power over serpents and scorpions" vs. "authority over serpents"
- **EMET:** "power over serpents"
- **LOGOS:** "authority over serpents"
- **PNEUMA:** "authority over serpents"
- **Note:** "Authority" (*exousia*) vs. "power" — theologically "authority" is more precise for *exousia*.

### v.12 — "preaching repentance and forgiveness"
- All agents agree. PNEUMA's tripled "we preached" is stylistic fragmentation.
- **Note:** PNEUMA's repetition ("We preached repentance. We preached forgiveness. We preached it in all the world") is literary addition beyond source.

---
*10 disagreements. SOPHIA: "still speaking" (v.1); "will be fulfilled" (v.3); "draw away" (v.4); "authority" over "power" (v.9); reject PNEUMA's stylistic fragmentations.*

---

## APE Summary
All 17 chapters of the Apocalypse of Peter are complete. Total files: 85 (17 × 5).
The hell-tour (chs.4–12) has been rendered with full sensory and theological weight.
The paradise vision (chs.13–14) with warmth and scriptural resonance.
The transfiguration sequence (chs.15–16) with christological precision.
The closing commission (ch.17) with canonical integration.
